headline_cluster.headline: אפקט אנבידיה: איך זה כשמנכ"ל אחד עוזב ג'נסן הואנג לא לבד: מחקר חדש בדק מה קורה לחברות במקרים שבהם מנכ"ל-על שנחשב לסופרסטאר פורש מתפקידו

extracted_claims: Study by Prof. Moran Ofir (Univ. of Haifa) and Prof. Yevgeny Mugerman (Bar-Ilan) on S&P 1500 CEO departures 2005-2024
2,501 total CEO departures; 204 'superstar' CEOs (~6% of sample); only 13 of the 204 were sudden/unplanned
Superstar CEO departure announcement day: stock fell ~1% on average
3 years post-departure: performance similar to comparable companies; profitability declined but not more than peers
If CEO stayed as chair/director: stock stable. If CEO left completely: avg drop ~3% vs ~1.3% for regular CEOs
3-year outcomes: Starbucks & Google beat market; Nike & Amazon lagged; Oracle moved with market
Nvidia: stock closed -4.3% day Huang's departure announced; sudden departures in study saw avg drops of 2-5% (Nvidia consistent with range)
Nvidia stock +34% in one day when Huang's return announced, adding >$1 trillion market value
Nvidia valued at ~$4 trillion at time of writing

Steve Jobs: resignation announced Aug 2011, named Tim Cook successor; stock +0.9% above market day 1; +~60% above market after 1 year; +~29% above market after 3 years; health announcements -2.5% same day; death (Oct 2011) -2.3%

auditor_refetch.author: איריס ליפשיץ-קליגר
missed_or_misparsed: Huang's exit described as abrupt, 'rather forced', amid a security investigation on suspicion of espionage; board initially said it would not reinstate him
Most of Nvidia's decline came AFTER the board said it would not reinstate him (not on the -4.3% resignation day); the +34% jump returned the stock to roughly the resignation-day close
Nvidia board said it consulted senior US government officials; reinstatement 'not a national security risk'
Superstar definition (Ofir): consistent market-beating record, OR founder / CEO >10 years, OR concurrent chair holding >=5% of shares; '~6% of CEOs in the study' met it
Internal arithmetic: 204/2,501 = 8.2%, not ~6% (unless 6% refers to a different base, e.g. all CEOs/CEO-years)
All 3-year comparison cases (Starbucks, Google, Nike, Amazon, Oracle): superstar stayed as chair/director
Elon Musk hypothetical section (not a factual claim)

primary_source_search: source_not_found: no paper/working paper/press release located. Searched EN+HE web, SSRN (author page 403), Google Scholar (Mugerman profile: no superstar-CEO/departure title), Haifa/Bar-Ilan news. Only secondary coverage found (ynet, ynetnews English mirror, fxtribune [403]) — all derive from the same ynet interview.

claims.claim_text: Study by Prof. Moran Ofir (Haifa) & Prof. Yevgeny Mugerman (Bar-Ilan) on S&P 1500 CEO departures, 2005-2024
claims.note: Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists. The authors are real and co-author regularly (SSRN/Scholar), but no superstar-CEO paper is listed.

claims.claim_text: 2,501 CEO departures, of which 204 were 'superstar' CEOs
claims.note: Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists.

claims.claim_text: Only ~6% of CEOs in the study met the superstar definition
claims.note: Internally inconsistent with the article's own counts unless the 6% uses a different base (e.g. all CEOs or CEO-years), which ynet doesn't say. Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists.

claims.claim_text: Only 13 of the 204 superstar departures were sudden/unexpected
claims.note: Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists.

claims.claim_text: Superstar departure announcement day: stock fell ~1% on average; 3 years later performance similar to peers; profitability fell but not more than peers
claims.note: Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists.

claims.claim_text: CEO stayed as chair/director: stock stable; left completely: ~-3% vs -1.3% for regular CEOs
claims.note: Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists.

claims.claim_text: Sudden departures in the study saw average drops of 2%-5%
claims.note: Primary paper not found (searched SSRN, Google Scholar, Haifa/Bar-Ilan, HE+EN web); only ynet-derived coverage exists. An 'average' stated as a range is itself imprecise wording.

claims.claim_text: Huang left abruptly and quite forcibly amid a security probe on suspicion of espionage (event reality)
claims.verified_figure: Real in news coverage: Huang resigned as CEO/president/director 12 Nov 2026 (Kress interim) amid affairs, one with a woman suspected of spying for China; reinstated 23 Nov 2026 (SEC 8-K)
claims.note: Event confirmed across multiple outlets plus Nvidia 8-K.

claims.claim_text: Nvidia stock closed -4.3% on the day of Huang's resignation
claims.verified_figure: Yahoo daily: 12 Nov 2026 close $166.19 vs $173.73 = -4.34% (intraday low $148.80, -14%)
claims.note: Close figure is correct. The intraday low was -14%, and the stock fell ~9% after hours the night before.

claims.claim_text: Nvidia's -4.3% is consistent with the study's sudden-departure drops of 2-5%
claims.verified_figure: Day-1 -4.34%; cumulative from pre-resignation close $173.73 to $125.53 on 20 Nov = -27.7%
claims.note: Comparing only the day-1 close understates the episode. The article itself notes most of the fall came after the board said it would not reinstate him (20 Nov: -14.0%). The study benchmark is unverifiable.

claims.claim_text: Most of Nvidia's decline came after the board said it wouldn't reinstate him; the +34% jump returned the stock to roughly the resignation-day close
Nvidia stock jumped 34% in one day on Huang's return, adding more than $1 trillion in value
claims.verified_figure: 23 Nov 2026 close-to-close +31.5% ($125.53 -> $165.05); ~24.1B shares -> ~$0.95T added; ~+34% was the morning intraday level (Fox Business); CNBC/Motley Fool: closed +31%, 'nearly $1 trillion'
claims.note: 34% was intraday, not the daily move; the close-to-close gain was ~31% and just under $1T.

claims.claim_text: Nvidia trades at ~$4 trillion (researcher quote)
claims.verified_figure: ~$3.98T at 23 Nov close; ~$3.6T at 25-27 Nov closes (Motley Fool: $3.63T on 27 Nov)
claims.note: Reasonable rounding for the week, if somewhat high by publication date (26 Nov).

claims.claim_text: Board said it consulted senior US government officials and that reinstatement poses no national-security risk
claims.verified_figure: Nvidia 8-K/press release 23 Nov 2026: 'received input from senior levels of the United States government', 'poses no national security risk'

claims.claim_text: Steve Jobs resigned Aug 2011 and named Tim Cook; AAPL +0.9% above market on first trading day
claims.note: Note that the raw move was negative; '+0.9% above market' is correctly phrased as relative.

claims.claim_text: AAPL ~60% above market one year after Jobs's resignation
claims.note: Roughly reproduces against the S&P 500; the exact benchmark/method is unknown.

claims.claim_text: AAPL ~29% above market three years after Jobs's resignation
claims.verified_figure: 24 Aug 2011->2014: AAPL +98.7% vs SPY +80.5% = +18.2pp (ratio +10.1%); vs Nasdaq-100 +2.5pp; vs XLK +19.9pp
claims.note: Could not reproduce ~29% against any standard benchmark (best ~+20pp). It may reflect an undisclosed abnormal-return model; the paper was not found.

claims.claim_text: Announcements about Jobs's health cut AAPL 2.5% in a day
Jobs's death (Oct 2011) cut the stock 2.3%
claims.note: The raw drop was only -0.23% (possibly a decimal slip). The ~-2% is a market-relative (abnormal) figure, but ynet presents it as an absolute fall and it doesn't match exactly (-2.0 vs -2.3).

claims.claim_text: Mark Parker's departure from Nike: stock -~4%
Larry Page's departure from Google: stock +~2%
claims.note: Accurate as a raw move (Alphabet CEO handover to Pichai).

claims.claim_text: 3-year outcomes: Starbucks & Google beat market, Nike & Amazon lagged, Oracle moved with market
claims.verified_figure: vs SPY total return: SBUX (from Dec 2016 / Apr 2017) +3.1pp / +2.8pp; GOOGL (Dec 2019) +18.2pp; NKE (Oct 2019) -38.4pp; AMZN (Feb/Jul 2021) -33.8pp / -25.6pp; ORCL (18 Sep 2014) +21.6% vs +32.2% = -10.6pp
claims.note: Four of five check out (Starbucks only marginally). Oracle lagged the S&P 500 by ~11pp rather than 'moving with' it. The claim that all stayed as chair/director: Schultz left Starbucks' board in June 2018, within the window.

note: Auditor: Huang exit/return is a real 2026 event (12 Nov resign, 23 Nov reinstated). Study figures unverifiable (paper not found). Market facts checked with Yahoo daily adjusted closes vs SPY. Red flags: Jobs-death -2.3% (misinterpreted).
